stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.description: I invented a chart mark for a ruin that people are still building, and that took me an afternoon. Defending it will take a year, because a mark with only one site under it looks like a mistake with a symbol on top. I've got to have two sites, or the survey office will file it as a special case and bury it. Bring me chips off the new four-faced stone the stonehands and stairwardens are carving, not the old grey. Then go and stand at the Green Cut, where somebody's been stacking our timber into something with a shape to it.
stn_a_mark_for_a_thing_still_being_made.accept_text: Bring the chips in a cloth. Fresh carving scratches if you let it knock about.

stn_a_name_at_the_other_end.description: A route isn't a route until somebody at the far end agrees to catch it. I've written my proposal out on both sides of a card, a timetable and a price, and the price is what he'll argue about. I've heard there's an orc on a tower in Hillsbrad who flies wyverns too and has nobody to fly them to. Take this to Wind-Rider Ghulrak at Tarren Mill. Fly up on the Baron's route and change at the mill, and yes, that means you're paying the fee I'm trying to stop paying.
stn_a_name_at_the_other_end.accept_text: Think about that fee for the whole flight, and you'll understand my position.

stn_cut_not_chewed.description: Pell's sawn stave has been on my table since dawn, and I've had it in my hand most of that time. My camp's losing crates every week, and now I know somebody's cutting them. The Zul'Marosh stonehands, the stone-armed trolls off the crag, have been working my road, and I want fewer of them on it. Then go and look at the Green Cut, where the road splits. That's where it stops being my road and starts being theirs.
stn_cut_not_chewed.accept_text: Don't bring me anything back from the Cut. Just tell me what you saw.

stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.description: I told the quartermaster to his face that the boots were bad. He wrote it down and nothing happened, because the only man who can condemn that batch is the one who signed for it. So I've given up on the boots and started working on the feet instead. There's a pale tuber in the rot of Rotvine Fen, as far east as the jungle goes before it turns to water, and it pulls the wet out of anything you pack it against. The fenrot creepers and sourwater oozes carry them. I can't condemn a boot, but I can keep a foot dry inside one.
stn_four_reports_and_a_boot.accept_text: The bloatspawn toads sit in the standing water out there. Watch where you step.

stn_hapka_still_counting.description: I've got four turned-away supply ships, a fen that stinks when it rains, and a cistern in the hill above it that's just started draining into my water. I don't care about the stair, I care about the smell. No berth-master will bring an airship down into that stink. The Rotvine sent one of their own, Hap'ka, to keep the stair for them, and he drowned doing it, and by every account that hasn't stopped him. Go down to the sump and finish him, and bring me whatever he's carrying.
stn_hapka_still_counting.accept_text: He's at the bottom of Rotvine Hollow. Breathe through your mouth on the way down.

stn_in_the_count.description: I once asked you, as a courtesy, not to look at the ground outside the west wall. I'm done asking for courtesies. The greenpelt panthers know which day we carry our dead out there, and thinning them buys a week, so kill a few more for me. Then take this to Innkeeper Rukha, who keeps a post with every name in this camp chalked on it, the only honest list of us there is. I want the ones outside the wall on it too, and I should have put that in a report two years ago.
stn_in_the_count.accept_text: Rukha won't make a fuss. Hand it to her and she'll know what to do.

stn_including_me.description: Everything in Grom'gol came off that airship, including me. In the camp's first season a crate of camp stores went over the side of the berth stair into Mistvale Lagoon, back when the mangroves still grew right up to the wall. The mistvale crocolisks moved in after, and they've dragged the bundles about. I want them back. They're stores, that's all they are, and I'd like them back before anybody else goes looking.
stn_including_me.accept_text: Watch the bloatspawn toads more than the crocs. Out there a toad looks like nothing until it's on you.

stn_keep_to_it.description: I hold Grom'gol's south gate. The greenpelt panthers have started sitting right outside it in broad daylight, and they aren't hunting the wall, they're waiting at it. I've kept the reason out of my reports. Thin them out around the gate and along the first bend of the road. Stay on the road while you do it, because there's nothing worth seeing off it on the west side.
stn_keep_to_it.accept_text: I'd take it as a kindness if you didn't go looking on the west side.

stn_less_wrong_than_it_was.description: I've drawn the Zul'Marosh crag three times, and each sheet has more stair on it than the last. I've assumed I miscounted, because the other explanation is a ruin that's getting bigger. Go east to the Zul'Marosh Steps and stand in the lower court, then go on to the way into Rotvine Hollow above it. Count the courses of stone in both. I've got three sheets with three different numbers on them, and every one of them is mine.
stn_less_wrong_than_it_was.accept_text: I don't want a rough guess, I want a number.

stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.description: Zul'Marosh is da oldest troll work in dis jungle. My own tribe has no story about buildin' it and no story about leavin' it, and a tribe with no story about a place was never dere. Da Rotvine call demselves keepers of dat stair, but dey're sittin' in someone else's house callin' demselves family. Dere vinespeakers carry knot-cords, which are records, and I want dem. I want you to hear me say it plain, I'm askin' you to take a people's writin' off dere bodies.
stn_nobody_left_who_built_it.accept_text: Dey're on da Zul'Marosh Steps, east of here, above da stairwardens.

stn_not_tame_fed.description: I keep da camp's raptor pens and wyvern lines, and I got one rule, mon: da animals ain't tame, dey're fed. Feed ran short da week da supply ship turned away, and now da greenpelt panthers have taken an interest in my pens. Dey sit in da green by da line and wait for feedin' time, same as da birds. I need good haunches off da rootgrubber boars, off da leg, not offal and not slop. A raptor dat gets slop remembers it, and den she bites da hand dat brought it.
stn_not_tame_fed.accept_text: Chase da panthers off too, before one works out which end has da gate.

stn_nothing_they_have_fought_climbs.description: I've got a drill ground, a palisade, and a training plan I've rewritten exactly once in my life, three years ago. Ask me why, and I'll tell you, because I'd rather you heard it here than worked it out on the Green Cut. Then go and fight something that climbs. The thornback apes east of the gate come down hand over hand, and they don't come at your front, they drop on your head. A recruit who's only ever been hit from the front dies looking at the ground.
stn_nothing_they_have_fought_climbs.accept_text: Ask me whatever you like first. Then go and get hit from above before I put anybody behind you.

stn_one_road_four_names.description: I've got the road on my map as the Vine Road, because that's what a camp full of orcs has called it for three years. Zul'jana tells me that's its fourth name, and the shortest. Nobody in Grom'gol has ever walked it from top to bottom, and I want it walked, so the map can carry an older name too. Start from the ground west of the Green Cut and go all the way south to where it runs into Central Stranglethorn. Zul'jana's promised me one of the older names once it's done, and only one.
stn_one_road_four_names.accept_text: Mind the coilvine pythons where the canopy comes down low. They hang right over the road.

stn_signed_for_twice.description: I've got a grant from Booty Bay with the Baron's stamp on it and a date written small underneath, and I've read it four times. It's a berth in the Baron's own harbour, granted to this camp for our airship, forever, at a price. Read the price, then read the little date under the stamp. That's not the day he signed it, it's the day he decided we'd one day have to come and ask. Take it across the camp to Overseer Mokra, because I know what it means and I don't want to be holding it when she finds out.
stn_signed_for_twice.accept_text: I've signed for everything that came off that stair, but I'm not signing for this.

stn_standing_water.description: I've got a ward full of men with rotting feet and a year of my own reports blaming the lagoon. I'd rather you didn't mention this to anyone. I need to know what that water does to a foot, from somebody who isn't one of my patients. Go south to Mistvale Lagoon and walk the shore, and kill enough of the mistvale crocolisks that you can stand in the water for a while. I'm not asking you to be careless, I'm asking you to tell me whether that water rots a foot in a week.
stn_standing_water.accept_text: Stand in it long enough to know. Then come and see me at the back of the tent, not the front.

stn_the_baron_charges_me_to_land.description: I pay Baron Revilgaz to land in Booty Bay, and I've paid it every week since the camp arrived. I want a second roost that isn't Booty Bay, and I've already picked the coast north of the camp, without having been to see it. Go up the coast trail past the ford, to the ground north-west of the Green Cut, and tell me if there's open sky over it. A wyvern wants water on one side and nothing overhead. Count the vinecrest raptors on the trail while you're at it, because I price a route by what eats the courier, not by how far it is.
stn_the_baron_charges_me_to_land.accept_text: You'll earn the look. Those raptors work that trail hard.

stn_the_hill_runs_warm.description: The water flowing out from under Rotvine Hollow is what rots the fen. I've put my hand in it twice to be sure of one odd thing, and it runs warm. Caves don't run warm, and less water's coming out of that hill than is standing inside it. Go into Rotvine Hollow as far as the first standing water and look at the waterline on the wall above it. I just need a yes or a no, whether there's more water in that hill than is coming out of it.
stn_the_hill_runs_warm.accept_text: Rotvine stranglers drop out of the roof. Keep your head up and your back to the stone.

stn_the_long_haul.description: There's no open sky on the coast north of here, which I learned at some cost to my dignity. So I've given up on a near roost, and we'll go in one long hop instead, over the water and up the whole coast to Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad. It's the longest route on any flight ledger in the Horde, and I'm already pricing it. A wyvern that flies that far can't eat on the way, so it needs pressed feed blocks. Get me boar fat and grain off the rootgrubber boars and thornback apes on the Green Cut, east of the gate.
stn_the_long_haul.accept_text: The apes have been raiding my feed store since the day it existed. Take some of it back.

stn_the_long_way_round.description: I came back round Rotvine Fen instead of through it, and I'd do it again. What I haven't told anyone is that I came back without my courier pouch, and the fen's had it for three weeks. This is a favour, and I'm asking it as one. My pouch is out on the causeway near the landing in Rotvine Fen, east of here, in the rot where the fenrot creepers sit. I haven't reported it, and I'd like to keep not reporting it.
stn_the_long_way_round.accept_text: Kill the creepers, and look where the gangplank meets the bank.

stn_the_other_half.description: I sell the half of the jungle that won't kill you. I buy my bark from a Darkspear supplier in Booty Bay who's started charging me a tariff, and the same bark grows a couple of hours' walk south of the gate, around Mistvale Lagoon. I need mangrove bark, stripped off the roots on the water side, not off the trunk. The camp calls it mistvale bark, which is wrong but shorter. The bloatspawn toads and the mangrove stiltstalkers pick the strips up when they root about, so take it off them.
stn_the_other_half.accept_text: The stiltstalkers don't rush, but they don't stop either, so keep moving.

stn_the_relay_signed.description: I've read a goblin's route, an orc's endorsement, and a note about weather in a jungle I'll never see. I'll light the tower, and not for the goblin or the orc, but for the bird, which has no say in any of this and is the one that'll hit the water. I've signed it, and I've added a line at the bottom in my own hand. In bad weather, the wyvern lands on my tower and the mail goes on by bat. Take this back to Pazzik at Grom'gol, and tell him that line isn't up for discussion.
stn_the_relay_signed.accept_text: He'll hate it. He'll sign it anyway, and you can watch him do both.

stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.description: I've climbed to the top of the Zul'Marosh Steps, and nobody in Grom'gol has asked me about it, because nobody believed the stair went anywhere. It leads to a flat court with a socket cut in the middle and nothing standing in it. The stairwardens hold the middle flights, east of here past the Green Cut, and they hold them properly, which I've never seen jungle trolls bother to do. Fight past the second landing and bring me loose course stone off the stair itself. I want to know what the stone can tell me about the top.
stn_the_stair_ends_in_a_socket.accept_text: The old grey stuff, from where it's fallen, not from where it's still laid.

stn_the_third_direction.description: I want a climbing frame on my drill ground, but every length of rope in Grom'gol's already been spliced twice. There's plenty of vine in this jungle, though, wrapped around something that doesn't like being shortened. Bring me coils of strangler vine, cut long and fresh off the wet ground where it's still green and hasn't gone woody. Clear the coilvine pythons off it first. Up in the canopy a python's exactly the colour of the vine you're reaching for, and you only make that mistake once.
stn_the_third_direction.accept_text: Long coils, mind. A short one's no good to anybody on a frame.

stn_the_weekly_shortfall.description: I count every crate into Grom'gol and every crate out, and for eleven weeks the numbers have come up short by the same amount. I've written it off as spoilage twice, and I didn't believe it either time. My tally says they go missing on the Vine Road, between our south gate and the first bend. Vinecrest raptors work that stretch, and raptors chew things. Walk the road back the other way, kill the raptors you find, and if you come across a chewed crate, bring me its staves.
stn_the_weekly_shortfall.accept_text: Look at the ends of the staves before you pick them up. I want to know what did the damage.

stn_three_flags.description: I raise two flags for an airship coming in and three for one that should keep flying. Three flags have gone up four times this season, each time with smoke rising over the fen, and the camp's gone a month short of supplies because of it. Smoke over the fen means fire, and fire in a jungle means a mooring nobody will risk. Go east to Rotvine Fen and find out what's burning. If it's those gas bladders the oozes and toads carry, bring me some, and I'll take the blame myself.
stn_three_flags.accept_text: The sourwater oozes are thick on that ground. Take the bladders off them, and off the toads.

stn_twelve_bunks_and_a_fire.description: I've got twelve bunks, a hearth, and the only dry wood in Grom'gol, which isn't dry. I need resin from the buttress trees to keep the fire going, because it burns even when it's wet, which is a small miracle. The rootgrubber boars dig it out of the bark and tread it into the mud, so you'll be taking it off them. And before you go, I don't care where you're from. Nobody behind this fence is from here, me included, and nobody else will tell you that, so I tell everyone early.
stn_twelve_bunks_and_a_fire.accept_text: Wrap it in leaves on the way back. It sticks to everything it touches.

stn_two_roosts_one_ledger.description: I know exactly what the middle of your goblin's route is, and it's open water with nowhere to land. I'll endorse it if somebody can cover that middle stretch, and the only ones who fly it at night are the Forsaken. There are things you should ask me before you fly anywhere, and I'll answer them, because a courier who doesn't know the route is just cargo. Then take my endorsement west to Bat Handler Odo at the Sepulcher, whose bats cross that water every night of the year. If he'll let a wyvern land on his tower in bad weather, the route stands.
stn_two_roosts_one_ledger.accept_text: If he won't, your goblin keeps paying his Baron. Ask me what you need to first.

stn_what_the_pens_know.description: My raptors have gone off dere feed on da same day every week since da dry season turned, and I stopped believin' it's da feed. A penned bird knows what's movin' on da road outside better dan da sentry does, and I been readin' mine for three seasons. Dis ain't somethin' I can hand you in a sack, and it ain't somethin' I'll carry to da overseer's table on my own. What I got is a shape in my head. A shape in one head is worth nothin' until someone else has heard it out loud and not laughed.
stn_what_the_pens_know.accept_text: Sit up on da rail and ask me. I'll tell you all of it.

stn_what_the_wood_is_for.description: I've rebuilt the same three things for three years, because nothing in this jungle dries out and every board in Grom'gol came off an airship. I heard what Mokra found at the Green Cut, and I already know what the trolls are doing with my wood. Bring me the battens they're cutting, the thin boards dressed to one length, off the Zul'Marosh stonehands and the thornback apes. If they're dressing boards, they aren't burning them. Watch the apes on the Green Cut, east of the gate, because they come for anything that smells of the camp.
stn_what_the_wood_is_for.accept_text: My lumber smells of the camp all the way through, so the apes will smell you coming, and that's fine.

stn_what_was_holding_it_back.description: I didn't need da second half of Hanzo's answer. Da Rotvine named da rot after dere hill, and dey were right to. Somethin' called Rootmaw is growin' across da throat of da lower gallery in Rotvine Hollow, a mass of roots with a mouth, and it's been drinkin' dat cistern since before anyone alive started countin'. Kill dat thing, and deal with da Zul'Marosh drowned down dere. Da drowned in dat hill ain't Rotvine, and dey never were.
stn_what_was_holding_it_back.accept_text: Look at da marks on da drowned before you take anything.
